name: Grus
introduction: is the Crane, a long-necked bird introduced by Dutch navigators in the 1590s. Its stars form a graceful line stretching from Piscis Austrinus toward the south celestial pole, best seen from the Southern Hemisphere in spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Grus shows clearly that stars have different colors. [Alnair](hip:109268) is a hot blue-white star, while [Tiaki](hip:112122) is a cool red giant; side by side, their colors contrast nicely to the naked eye.
The pair [Delta¹ Gruis](hip:110997) and Delta² Gruis is an optical double: two giants that look close together but lie at different distances.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alnair](hip:109268), 101 light-years away, is the brightest star. [Aldhanab](hip:108085) is a blue-white subgiant. Nearby in space, [Gliese 832](id:10pc-0103), a red dwarf 16 light-years away, hosts a giant planet.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Grus lies far from the Milky Way, toward galaxy groups such as the Grus Quartet, four interacting galaxies tugging at each other.
